name: Late Infantile Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis Type 1

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Late Infantile Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis Type 1

criteria.description: Progressive psychomotor regression with onset between 1 and 4 years of age
Demonstration of deficient palmitoyl-protein thioesterase 1 (PPT1) enzyme activity in leukocytes or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic variants in the CLN1 (PPT1) gene
Brain MRI showing cerebral and cerebellar atrophy
Detection of characteristic granular osmiophilic deposits in peripheral blood lymphocytes or skin biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive psychomotor regression with onset between 1 and 4 years plus either deficient PPT1 enzyme activity or identification of pathogenic CLN1 mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by biochemical and genetic testing; neuroimaging and ultrastructural studies support diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Loss of previously acquired motor and cognitive skills

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visual loss due to retinal degeneration
pathognomonic.notes: Progressive vision impairment leading to blindness
searchTerms: loss of sight due to retina problems

common.notes: Reduced muscle tone contributing to motor delay
Loss of previously acquired language skills

occasional.notes: Involuntary muscle contractions causing abnormal postures

rare.notes: Mild enlargement of liver and spleen
Swelling of extremities in late stages

laboratory: Reduced palmitoyl-protein thioesterase 1 (PPT1) enzyme activity in leukocytes or fibroblasts
Elevated levels of lipofuscin-like storage material in peripheral blood lymphocytes
imaging: Brain MRI showing cerebral and cerebellar atrophy
Thinning of corpus callosum and ventricular enlargement
other: Electron microscopy revealing granular osmiophilic deposits in skin or conjunctival biopsy

distinguishingFeatures: Deficiency of tripeptidyl peptidase 1 (TPP1) enzyme instead of PPT1
Later onset (2-4 years) with more prominent seizures
Different genetic mutations in CLN2 gene
Prominent visual loss as initial symptom

redFlags: Rapidly progressive psychomotor regression in early childhood
Early onset refractory seizures with myoclonic jerks
Progressive visual loss leading to blindness
references: Mole SE, Williams RE. Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinoses. Oxford Monographs on Medical Genetics. 2003.
The International NCL Database Consortium. Clinical and molecular features of CLN1 disease. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases. 2020.
Williams RE, Mole SE. New nomenclature and classification scheme for the neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses. Neurology. 2012.
